trust_decision.summary: addHeaders decides which client-listed Connection (hop-by-hop) tokens to keep. Only tokens in the hard-coded protectHeaders set are dropped, so the operator-configured RequestID/ClientIPHeader/TLSHeader names stay listed, and httputil.ReverseProxy then deletes the values fabio set.

landing_point.why: The prior CVE-2025-48865 fix lives here: the protectHeaders lookup over Connection tokens is the obvious place to extend.

fix_sites.entry_point: same; protect list renamed and exported as DefaultProtectHeaders (fix.diff:42-44)
same; addHeaders signature gains the hdrs map (fix.diff:56)
public API struct proxy.HTTPProxy gains a ProtectHeaders field (fix.diff:293-294)
fabio startup newHTTPProxy: merges cfg.Proxy.RequestID/ClientIPHeader/TLSHeader into the protect map (fix.diff:17-21)
fabio startup: ProtectHeaders wired into HTTPProxy (fix.diff:30)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: main.go:186-241 (fix adds the config-to-protect-list merge at fix.diff:17-21). It is not required: a solver can read cfg.RequestID/ClientIPHeader/TLSHeader inside addHeaders, which already receives cfg (proxy/http_headers.go:45).

O3_reason_to_dismiss: "The TLS header is deleted on non-TLS requests anyway (proxy/http_headers.go:155), so stripping it is harmless", or "RequestID is just a tracing ID, not a trust header". Both are weak, because the advisory names all three headers.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Client-listed non-protected hop-by-hop tokens (e.g. legit custom headers, keep-alive) must still be honoured and stripped. A fix that drops the whole Connection header or ignores its tokens breaks this.

O6_input_shapes: comma-separated tokens in one Connection header value
case variants of the token (CanonicalMIMEHeaderKey on both token and configured name)

O7_producer.where: config/load.go:149-152 (proxy.header.clientip/tls/requestid flags define the names that must be protected)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An extra operator-configured header (e.g. a configurable X-Forwarded-Prefix name or a client-cert/SNI header) that addHeaders sets but that is never added to the protect list.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: addHeaders already sets several config-named headers; a maintainer adding one more would add the Set and forget the Connection protect list, which sits 40 lines higher.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A websocket path that rebuilds Connection/Upgrade itself before r.Write and re-adds client tokens unfiltered.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The WS path bypasses httputil.ReverseProxy and writes the raw request, so a maintainer normalising the Upgrade handshake there could plausibly copy client Connection tokens back.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: gRPC metadata forwarding (md.Copy) with fabio-injected client-ip metadata that a client-supplied key could shadow or remove.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The gRPC director forwards all incoming metadata verbatim; adding a client-ip metadata key here would mirror the HTTP feature.

O9_family: trust-header spoofing/stripping via hop-by-hop Connection header (CWE-290/CWE-348, incomplete prior fix)

O10_build.project_tests: proxy/http_headers_test.go (TestAddHeaders), proxy/http_integration_test.go:44-82 (TestProxyProducesCorrectXForwardedSomethingHeader) via httptest; run without Consul

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Inside addHeaders, also skip Connection tokens equal to cfg.RequestID/ClientIPHeader/TLSHeader (canonicalised). This is a fully correct fix, so the task gives no scope trap.

out_of_scope_notes: The published fix aliases and mutates the global proxy.DefaultProtectHeaders map (fix.diff:18-21), and a library user who builds proxy.HTTPProxy without ProtectHeaders gets a nil map, which drops even the original CVE-2025-48865 protection (fix.diff:65, fix.diff:303).
Route access rules (t.AccessDeniedHTTP, proxy/http_proxy.go:108) run on client-supplied headers before addHeaders; this is a separate trust question and was not pursued.
